title: Finite-presentation module continuity for affine limits of spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is of finite presentation if etale locally it has an exact presentation $\mathcal O_X^m\to\mathcal O_X^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. For a morphism $a:X\to Y$ use tensor pullback $a^*M=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{a^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}a^{-1}M$ for the canonical morphism of ringed etale topoi [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and $(X_i,q_{ji})$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces with affine transition maps $q_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$ for $j\ge i$, and limit $X$ with projections $q_i$. Here quasi-compact means admitting a surjective etale chart from a quasi-compact scheme, quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact, and affine means representable with affine source after pullback to every affine scheme test; a representable map is quasi-compact when its inverse images of affine scheme tests are quasi-compact. Tensor pullback preserves finite presentation. Every finitely presented module $M$ on $X$ is isomorphic to $q_i^*M_i$ for some $i$ and finitely presented $M_i$ on $X_i$. For fixed finitely presented $F_i,G_i$ on $X_i$, every map $q_i^*F_i\to q_i^*G_i$ is the pullback of a map $q_{ji}^*F_i\to q_{ji}^*G_i$ for some $j\ge i$. Two maps between fixed finitely presented modules on one stage that become equal on $X$ are equal after pullback to some later stage. All comparisons of iterated pullbacks use the canonical composition isomorphisms.

proof.text: First record the site conventions needed below. A finite presentation is a quasi-coherent presentation with finite index sets, so every finitely presented module is quasi-coherent. On a scheme, the Zariski/small-etale equivalence preserves and reflects finite presentation by the exact-finiteness comparison. Its natural pullback comparison identifies scheme tensor pullback with tensor pullback between small etale topoi. Consequently a finitely presented module on an etale scheme chart gives a finitely presented ordinary scheme module, and conversely. For a surjective etale atlas, finite presentation is detected on its pullback: the enlarged-site model identifies this pullback with localization, and presentations on a covering of the atlas are precisely presentations on a covering of the space. This last assertion uses the definition of finite presentation, not a claim that arbitrary inverse image is exact.

For any $a:Y\to Z$ of algebraic spaces and finitely presented $N$ on $Z$, choose a jointly surjective etale scheme family $V_b\to Z$ carrying finite presentations of $N$. Cover each $Y\times_Z V_b$ by etale schemes $W_{bc}$. The composites $W_{bc}\to Y$ cover $Y$ by etale base change and composition. Write $h_{bc}:W_{bc}\to V_b$. On $W_{bc}$ the restriction of $a^*N$ is $h_{bc}^*(N|_{V_b})$: both are tensor pullback along the same composite to $Z$, using the composition and localization comparisons in the enlarged-site model. By step 1, $N|_{V_b}$ is a finitely presented Zariski module. Scheme tensor pullback preserves finite presentation, without flatness, so $h_{bc}^*(N|_{V_b})$ is finitely presented. The scheme comparison and locality from step 1 now give finite presentation of $a^*N$. This proves the pullback clause, including all transition and projection pullbacks used below.

source.place: Tag 03DO (lemma-local-pullback), clause (7), proved here by reduction to scheme charts

proof.text: Choose $0\in I$ and restrict to the directed cofinal tail $i\geq0$. The tail is cofinal since for each $k$ there is $j\geq0,k$; compatible tail maps extend uniquely to $k$ by composition, independently of $j$ by directedness. Choose an affine surjective etale atlas $U_0\to X_0$. Set $U_i=X_i\times_{X_0}U_0$, $R_i=U_i\times_{X_i}U_i$ and $T_i=U_i\times_{X_i}U_i\times_{X_i}U_i$. The affine-locality theorem makes each $U_i$ affine, since $X_i\to X_0$ is affine. Fibre-product representability makes $R_i,T_i$ schemes. The qcqs fibre-product theorem uses point-space quasi-compactness: $X_i$ and $U_i$ (affine, so qcqs) have quasi-compact point spaces by the continuous-surjection clause of the finite-subatlas lemma, and quasi-separatedness is the same diagonal test. Applied to $U_i\times_{X_i}U_i$, then $R_i\times_{X_i}U_i$, it makes $R_i,T_i$ qcqs in that sense; the affine-atlas lemma gives surjective etale maps from affine schemes, so these schemes are quasi-compact, and the diagonal test on affine opens makes them quasi-separated. Transition maps of all three systems are base changes of $X_j\to X_i$, hence affine. More explicitly $R_i=X_i\times_{X_0}R_0$ and $T_i=X_i\times_{X_0}T_0$: a test map on either side specifies the same ordered pairs or triples of atlas lifts with one common map to $X_i$. The space-limit theorem makes $X\to X_0$ affine, so $X\times_{X_0}U_0\to U_0$ is affine and $X\times_{X_0}U_0$ is an affine scheme by affine-locality. Its base-change clause therefore gives $U=\lim U_i=X\times_{X_0}U_0$, $R=\lim R_i=U\times_XU$ and $T=\lim T_i=U\times_XU\times_XU$. These are scheme limits, testing on schemes. Projections, identity and composition maps are the coordinate maps, compatible with these identifications. The map $U\to X$ is surjective etale by base change.

proof.text: Let $M$ be finitely presented on $X$. The groupoid equivalence associates to it the quasi-coherent scheme module $A=M|_U$ with an isomorphism $\alpha:t^*A\simeq s^*A$ on $R$, identity on the diagonal and satisfying the composition equation on $T$. Here $t=\operatorname{pr}_0$, $s=\operatorname{pr}_1$; thus on a triple $(u_0,u_1,u_2)$ the equation is $\alpha_{02}=\alpha_{12}\circ\alpha_{01}$. Step 1 makes $A$ finitely presented as an ordinary scheme module. Apply clause (1) of scheme module continuity to $U=\lim U_i$ to obtain a finitely presented $A_i$ on $U_i$ and a specified isomorphism of its limit pullback with $A$. Transport $\alpha$ through this isomorphism and the canonical pullback comparisons; retain its inverse $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$. All their sources and targets are pullbacks of $A_i$, hence finitely presented by step 2.

source.place: Tag 07V7 (lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation), application of limits.tex Tag 01ZR (lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation) to U and R

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of scheme module continuity on $R=\lim R_j$ to lift both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ between the fixed modules $t_i^*A_i,s_i^*A_i$. Directedness places both lifts $a,b$ at one stage. Their composites pull back to identities, so clause (3), twice on the relation scheme system, makes $ba=1$ and $ab=1$ after a further common stage. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism. Let $e_j:U_j\to R_j$ be the diagonal and let $p_{kl}:T_j\to R_j$ select vertices $k,l$. On $U$ the maps $e_j^*a$ and $1$ agree. On $T$ the maps $p_{02}^*a$ and $p_{12}^*a\circ p_{01}^*a$ agree. Their finite-stage sources and targets are fixed pullbacks of the finitely presented $A_j$; scheme pullback preserves finite presentation. Clause (3) applied to $U=\lim U_j$ and $T=\lim T_j$ gives a later stage $k$ where both equations hold. Earlier equations persist under further pullback because a functor preserves composition and identity. We have therefore obtained a genuine groupoid module $(A_k,a_k)$, including its identity, inverse and cocycle equations, whose limit datum is the specified datum of $M$.

source.place: Tag 07V7 (lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation), last sentence expanded using limits.tex Tag 01ZR (2),(3) on U, R and composable pairs

proof.text: Apply the groupoid equivalence at stage $k$ to $(A_k,a_k)$ to obtain a quasi-coherent module $M_k$ on $X_k$. Its atlas restriction is $A_k$. Step 1 and the etale-local definition make $M_k$ finitely presented, since $A_k$ is finitely presented. Pulling back its datum to $U,R$ gives the datum of $M$: the atlas module comparison is the chosen isomorphism, and the relation-map comparison is the prescribed equality $a_k|_R=\alpha$. The canonical composition comparisons give these identifications, since each of the two ways to pull back is pullback along the same composite to $X_k$. Full faithfulness of the groupoid equivalence on $X$ lifts the datum isomorphism and its inverse to inverse module maps, hence $q_k^*M_k\simeq M$. This proves object descent.

source.place: Tag 07V7 (lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation), equivalences with groupoid modules; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M3 (proposition-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: For the map clause start at the specified index $i$ and repeat the atlas construction there. Restrict $F_i,G_i$ to finitely presented scheme modules $B_i,C_i$ on $U_i$, with their canonical relation isomorphisms $\alpha_{F,i},\alpha_{G,i}$. A prescribed map $u:q_i^*F_i\to q_i^*G_i$ gives a map $v:B\to C$ commuting with the relation data. Scheme continuity (2) on $U$ lifts $v$ to $v_j:B_j\to C_j$. On $R_j$ compare the two parallel maps $\alpha_{G,j}\circ t_j^*v_j$ and $s_j^*v_j\circ\alpha_{F,j}$ from $t_j^*B_j$ to $s_j^*C_j$. Their limit pullbacks agree, and their sources and targets are finitely presented. Scheme continuity (3) on $R$ therefore makes them equal at a later stage $k$. Fullness of the groupoid equivalence on $X_k$ gives the unique module map $q_{ki}^*F_i\to q_{ki}^*G_i$ whose atlas restriction is $v_k$. Its limit pullback has the same atlas restriction as $u$, and faithfulness on $X$ makes it equal to $u$. All comparisons here are the canonical composition comparisons, so this is descent of the specified map between the fixed models.

source.place: Tag 07V7 (lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation), formal full-faithfulness argument; limits.tex Tag 01ZR (2),(3)

proof.text: Finally, let $u_i,v_i:F_i\to G_i$ have equal limit pullbacks. Restrict them to $U_i$. Their pullbacks to $U$ agree; clause (3) of scheme module continuity on $U=\lim U_j$ gives $k\geq i$ where the two atlas maps agree. Faithfulness of the groupoid equivalence on $X_k$ implies $q_{ki}^*u_i=q_{ki}^*v_i$. This proves eventual equality. The same argument includes empty spaces and zero modules; no projection was assumed surjective, only the base-changed atlas was.
